title: Mode 3 (free-cadence lockstep) at certificate level: GroundedCertLock with a one-counter threaded state, history reconstruction, certificate-level pinning, and lockstep_recent_certified_suffix_agreement by transport through the existing full-chain lockstep engine
goal_statement: Deliver the certificate presentation of mode 3 additively. A new inductive GroundedCertLock (n) (Signed) (G) : CertClaim → Nat → Prop mirrors GroundedCertSched but replaces the scheduled pin by the no-mixing fold check against ONE threaded Nat g = the prefix tip's declared generation: each fold checks g ≤ b.keyIndex and (cl.tipSlot / n = b.slot / n → g = b.keyIndex), then sets the state to b.keyIndex. A Bool suffix check lockstepFrom n tipSlot g suffix (the analogue of keyMonoFrom / schedPinned-over-the-suffix) runs the same two-clause check along the suffix. The reconstruction lemma groundedCertLock_suffix_history rebuilds a full chain that is validChain-accepted, lockstepOk, G-rooted and blockwise Signed; since lockstepOk implies keyMonoOk (new lemma keyMonoOk_of_lockstepOk), the reconstructed SignedChain passes the FULL validSignedChainLock, so every existing full-chain lockstep theorem applies verbatim. Answers to the four questions: (1) Pinning cannot be GATED at fold time -- rosterGen is execution-level and unknown to any verifier -- but it is DERIVED at fold-state level: the fold carries exactly the state the no-mixing rule needs (tipSlot, already in the claim, plus the tip generation g), and the certificate-level pinning theorems (lockstep_cert_declares_rosterGen for every tail/suffix block in a matured grid window; lockstep_cert_gen_pinned for the certificate's own g once its grid window is matured by the suffix) are corollaries of lockstep_declares_rosterGen applied to the reconstructed recent full chain. No per-window generation table, no running counter, no lagged counter is carried: the lagged counter lagSched is proof-internal (the transport lockstep_validSignedChainSched), never wire data. (2) Transporting unchanged from the mode-2 certificate path: exists_signedChain_of_covered, validChain_append_suffix, windowCount_append, windowCount_filter_low, validChain_append_one, slot_le_tip_of_mem, strictSlots_of_checks, linksOk_isChain, blockAt_getLast, validChain_sound, and the consumer chain sched_deep_block_agreement_of_length + schedUnforgeable_of_core + packageA_byzantine_bounded, plus the lockstep engine lockstep_declares_rosterGen / lockstep_validSignedChainSched / LockstepPackage.toPackageA. NOT transportable: groundedCertSched_history / groundedCertSched_suffix_history (different inductive; their proofs are copied with the pin conjunct replaced by lockstepOk maintenance) and sched_recent_certified_suffix_agreement itself (its GroundedCertSched inputs at lagSched cannot be produced: the verifier does not know rosterGen, and intermediate prefixes are not recent so the EUF-CMA surface would not cover a per-fold pin). The agreement theorem is therefore a direct proof that routes: reconstruct -> lockstep_validSignedChainSched (full chain, once, at the recent tip) -> sched_deep_block_agreement_of_length at schedule lagSched n rosterGen with k := c.length + i -- i.e. the same consumer sched_recent_certified_suffix_agreement closes with. (3) The LockstepPackage budget needs NO restating: rentBound/exposedBound/budget_le are chain-independent (badSched at lagSched reads no chain), so the certificate theorem takes hP : LockstepPackage unchanged, with no AttestedHistory quantification (the mode-1 complication) -- the same simplification mode 2's certificate form enjoyed. (4) Beyond the plain claim the certificate attests the tip generation g ('claim and generation together', the one-Nat analogue of GroundedCertK's n-vector floor); and for n ≥ 2 this is provably redundant (groundedCertLock_gen_of_tail: the tip block is the last element of cl.tail, so g is a function of the claim and the joint-authentication contract is met by the claim alone); only n = 1 (empty tail) genuinely needs the extra counter. Unauthenticated g would be a real attack (g* = 0 lets a suffix block signed under a stolen retired-generation key pass, exactly mode 2's schedule* ≡ 0 attack), so the docstring records the wire contract as GroundedCertK's does.

new_defs.name: MoltPetit.Model.lockstepFrom
new_defs.signature:
def lockstepFrom (n : Nat) : Nat → Nat → Chain → Bool
  | _, _, [] => true
  | ts, g, b :: rest =>
      decide (g ≤ b.keyIndex ∧ (ts / n = b.slot / n → g = b.keyIndex))
      && lockstepFrom n b.slot b.keyIndex rest
new_defs.meaning: The suffix-side no-mixing check a certificate-syncing verifier runs: fold the boundary state (tipSlot, tip generation) through the suffix; each block must not decrease the generation and must equal it when it lies in the same grid window (slot / n) as the current state block; the state then becomes (b.slot, b.keyIndex). Analogue of keyMonoFrom (KeyStealingCert.lean:159) with a single Nat instead of an n-vector, and of schedPinned-over-the-suffix in mode 2. Pure function of (tipSlot, g, suffix).

new_defs.name: MoltPetit.Model.GroundedCertLock
new_defs.signature:
inductive GroundedCertLock (n : Nat) (Signed : Block → Prop) (G : Block) : CertClaim → Nat → Prop
  | genesis : genesisOk G = true → G.slot = 0 → Signed G →
      GroundedCertLock n Signed G { tipId := G.id, tipSlot := G.slot, tipHeight := G.height, tail := [G].filter fun x => decide (G.slot + 2 - n ≤ x.slot) } G.keyIndex
  | extend (cl : CertClaim) (g : Nat) (b : Block) :
      GroundedCertLock n Signed G cl g → b.height = cl.tipHeight + 1 → cl.tipSlot < b.slot → b.prev = some cl.tipId → Signed b →
      g ≤ b.keyIndex → (cl.tipSlot / n = b.slot / n → g = b.keyIndex) →
      (∀ u : Nat, cl.tipSlot + 2 ≤ u + n → u + n ≤ b.slot + 1 → quorum n ≤ windowCount (cl.tail ++ [b]) u n) →
      GroundedCertLock n Signed G { tipId := b.id, tipSlot := b.slot, tipHeight := b.height, tail := (cl.tail ++ [b]).filter fun x => decide (b.slot + 2 - n ≤ x.slot) } b.keyIndex
new_defs.meaning: The lockstep certificate derivation: GroundedCertSched's shape (KeyStealingScheduleCert.lean:371; genesis must be Signed, same tail shape and Nat-form density premise so the standard windowCount_append/windowCount_filter_low rewrite transfers) with the pin premise replaced by the two-clause no-mixing check against the threaded tip generation g, and the state stepped to b.keyIndex. Every check is a pure function of (claim, g, block) -- what a recursive circuit attests per fold. The genesis state is G.keyIndex (the counter's initial value, matching LockstepPackage.genesis_gen).

new_defs.name: MoltPetit.Model.GroundedHistoryLock
new_defs.signature:
structure GroundedHistoryLock (n : Nat) (Signed : Block → Prop) (G : Block) (cl : CertClaim) (g : Nat) (c : Chain) : Prop where
  valid     : validChain n c = true
  lock      : lockstepOk n c = true
  head      : blockAt? c 0 = some G
  tip       : ∃ t : Block, c.getLast? = some t ∧ t.id = cl.tipId ∧ t.slot = cl.tipSlot ∧ t.height = cl.tipHeight ∧ t.keyIndex = g
  tail_eq   : cl.tail = c.filter fun x => decide (cl.tipSlot + 2 - n ≤ x.slot)
  len_eq    : c.length = cl.tipHeight + 1
  signed    : ∀ B ∈ c, Signed B
  gen_max   : ∀ B ∈ c, B.keyIndex ≤ g
  win_const : ∀ B ∈ c, B.slot / n = cl.tipSlot / n → B.keyIndex = g
new_defs.meaning: What a GroundedCertLock derivation reconstructs: GroundedHistorySched's fields (KeyStealingScheduleCert.lean:396) with `pinned` replaced by `lock`, the tip additionally carrying keyIndex = g, and two invariants (every prefix block's generation ≤ g; every prefix block in the tip's grid window declares g) that make the extend step purely arithmetic (no positional reasoning about the tip inside c).

new_theorems.proof_sketch: rw [keyMonoOk_iff_pairwise]; exact ((lockstepOk_iff_pairwise c).mp h).imp (fun hab _ => hab.2). new_theorems.name: MoltPetit.Model.lockstepOk_append_of_from
hypotheses: {n : Nat} {c s : Chain} {ts g : Nat}
(hLock : lockstepOk n c = true)
(hSlots : ∀ a ∈ c, a.slot ≤ ts)
(hMax : ∀ a ∈ c, a.keyIndex ≤ g)
(hConst : ∀ a ∈ c, a.slot / n = ts / n → a.keyIndex = g)
(hGt : ∀ b ∈ s, ts < b.slot)
(hSS : StrictSlots s)
(hFrom : lockstepFrom n ts g s = true)
new_theorems.proof_sketch: Induction on s generalizing c ts g. nil: simpa. cons b rest: unfold lockstepFrom; Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq give hb : g ≤ b.keyIndex ∧ (ts / n = b.slot / n → g = b.keyIndex) and hrest. Rewrite c ++ b :: rest = (c ++ [b]) ++ rest (List.append_cons / simp). Step 1: lockstepOk n (c ++ [b]) via lockstepOk_append_iff: left hLock, right trivial (singleton), cross for a ∈ c: a.keyIndex ≤ g ≤ b.keyIndex; if a.slot / n = b.slot / n then from a.slot ≤ ts < b.slot and Nat.div_le_div_right, a.slot / n ≤ ts / n ≤ b.slot / n, so ts / n = b.slot / n, hence g = b.keyIndex (hb.2) and a.keyIndex = g (hConst, since a.slot / n = ts / n) -- omega closes. Step 2: apply IH with c := c ++ [b], ts := b.slot, g := b.keyIndex: hSlots' (members of c: ≤ ts < b.slot; b: le_refl), hMax' (≤ g ≤ b.keyIndex; b: le_refl), hConst' (a ∈ c with a.slot / n = b.slot / n → a.keyIndex = g = b.keyIndex by the same sandwich; b: rfl), hGt' and hSS' from List.pairwise_cons.mp hSS. Serves BOTH the one-block fold step of groundedCertLock_history (s := [b]) and the suffix attachment. ~55 lines.

new_theorems.proof_sketch: obtain ⟨c, hist⟩ := groundedCertLock_history (by omega) h; t from hist.tip is a member of c (List.mem_of_getLast? / List.getLast?_eq_some_iff); rw [hist.tail_eq]; List.mem_filter.mpr ⟨ht, decide_eq_true (by omega : cl.tipSlot + 2 - n ≤ t.slot)⟩ using t.slot = cl.tipSlot and n ≥ 2. new_theorems.proof_sketch: Hypothesis list = sched_recent_certified_suffix_agreement's with (hUnf, hHash, hBudget, schedule) replaced by hP and (hPinS, GroundedCertSched) by (hLockS, GroundedCertLock … g). Proof: groundedCertLock_signedChain twice → sc, sc' with stripSigs sc = c ++ s₁ :: srest, validSignedChainLock, hHead, hfullTip, hLen. Transport once, at the recent full chain: hValS := lockstep_validSignedChainSched hn hP hValL hHead ⟨sTip, hfullTip, hRecent⟩ : validSignedChainSched n (lagSched n rosterGen) ops registry sc = true (and primed). Global index: hBfull : blockAt? (stripSigs sc) (c.length + i) = some B by rw [hstrip]; unfold blockAt?; List.getElem?_append_right; hkEq : c'.length + i' = c.length + i by omega from hLen/hLen'/hHeight (copied from KeyStealingScheduleCert.lean:672-685). Close: sched_deep_block_agreement_of_length hn (schedUnforgeable_of_core hP.toPackageA.unforgeable) hP.hashInj (packageA_byzantine_bounded hP.toPackageA) hValS hValS' hHead hHead' ⟨sTip, hfullTip, hRecent⟩ ⟨sTip', hfullTip', hRecent'⟩ (k := c.length + i) hBfull hB'full (by rw [hstrip, List.length_append]; omega) (by rw [hstrip', List.length_append]; omega). The schedule binder is lagSched n rosterGen throughout -- proof-internal, never verifier data. Budget: hP unchanged, chain-independent, no AttestedHistory. ~60 lines.

risks.mitigation: State the sandwich as a separate 5-line lemma (a ≤ ts → ts < b → a / n = b / n → ts / n = b / n ∧ a / n = ts / n) proved via Nat.div_le_div_right + Nat.le_antisymm, then everything else is omega on plain Nats. The gen_max/win_const invariants were chosen precisely so no dropLast/position reasoning about the tip is needed.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Read the tip generation from cl.tail at fold time (no threaded state; the fold checks no-mixing against every tail block).
alternatives_rejected.why: For n = 1 the tail is empty, so cross-window monotonicity against the prefix tip would go unchecked and lockstepOk of the reconstructed chain would be unprovable; a uniform threaded Nat is simpler to induct on and is provably redundant for n ≥ 2 (groundedCertLock_gen_of_tail), which gives the same zero-wire-cost result without a 2 ≤ n restriction.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Derive a GroundedCertSched at lagSched n rosterGen from GroundedCertLock and invoke sched_recent_certified_suffix_agreement literally.
alternatives_rejected.why: Impossible for the verifier (rosterGen is execution-level, never wire data) and unsound as a proof strategy: a per-fold pin at lagSched would need lockstep_declares_rosterGen on every intermediate prefix, but the EUF-CMA surface covers only RECENT chains; intermediate prefixes are not recent. Pinning must be applied once, to the full reconstructed chain with the recent suffix tip -- which is exactly what routing through lockstep_validSignedChainSched then sched_deep_block_agreement_of_length does.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Re-prove the pinning census at certificate level (a cert-level lockstep_declares_rosterGen with its own counting).
alternatives_rejected.why: Unnecessary: the reconstruction yields a full chain with genesis at index 0 and a recent tip, so the existing theorem applies unchanged; a re-proof would duplicate 170 lines and the private helpers.

alternatives_rejected.alt: A core lockstep validator (drop keyMonoOk) with core mirrors of the lockstep theorems, mirroring the mode-2 certificate path.
alternatives_rejected.why: Not needed: lockstepOk (roster-wide monotone) implies keyMonoOk (same-producer monotone), so the FULL validSignedChainLock is reconstructible from certificate data; no core variant and no mirrors.

alternatives_rejected.alt: State the suffix check as (boundary check on s₁) ∧ lockstepOk n (s₁ :: srest) instead of the lockstepFrom fold.
alternatives_rejected.why: Logically equivalent, but the fold is what a verifier runs, mirrors keyMonoFrom (KeyStealingCert.lean:159) and the TS bridge shape (keyMonoFromTs), and gives the one-block fold step of the history proof for free (s := [b]).

alternatives_rejected.alt: Restate the LockstepPackage budget over attestable histories (AttestedHistory-style, as mode 1's keyrot cert theorem).
alternatives_rejected.why: badSched at lagSched reads no chain and LockstepPackage's rentBound/exposedBound are chain-independent, so the package is consumed verbatim; quantifying over histories would only weaken the statement for no gain.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Put the axiom guards inside the new module instead of a separate guard file.
alternatives_rejected.why: Owner's constraint prefers a new guard file; one per library keeps the Results/Axioms.lean and Molt/Axioms.lean discipline visible in the tree.
